title: Digital Logic Design
description: Circuit theory (Kirchhoff's laws, Thevenin's and Norton's theorems), semiconductors, diodes and transistors, logic families and logic gates, combinational logic and the standard SOP and POS forms, minimisation with Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps and the Quine-McCluskey method, standard combinational circuits, and sequential circuits, registers, counters, computer codes and error detection. Built from the CSC 213 course book (Digital Logic Design, Nancy C. Woods) and the lecture slides in the course folder.

topics.title: Basic Circuit Theory
topics.summary: An electric circuit is a closed loop through which current can flow, analysed with Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws. Thevenin's and Norton's theorems reduce any linear circuit to a single source with one resistance.

topics.title: Semiconductors, Diodes and Transistors
topics.summary: Semiconductors have conductivity between conductors and insulators; doping makes N-type and P-type material, and a P-N junction makes a diode. Transistors are three-terminal devices: the current-operated BJT and the voltage-operated FET.
subtopics: The P-N junction, depletion region and biasing
Bipolar junction transistors and the transistor as a switch
Field effect transistors: JFET and MOSFET

topics.title: Logic Families and Logic Gates
topics.summary: Integrated circuits are grouped by scale of integration and into logic families, mainly TTL and CMOS, compared by voltage levels, noise margin, propagation delay and fan-out. Logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR) are the building blocks of digital circuits; NAND and NOR are universal.
subtopics: Scales of integration: SSI to ULSI and SoC
Noise immunity, noise margin, propagation delay and fan-out
The basic logic gates and their truth tables

topics.title: Combinational Logic and Standard Forms
topics.summary: A combinational logic circuit's output depends only on its present inputs; it is specified by a truth table, a Boolean expression or a logic diagram. Standard forms are the sum of products (SOP) and product of sums (POS), with minterms and maxterms in the fundamental (canonical) forms.
subtopics: Logic circuit diagrams and evaluating outputs
Product terms and sum of products
Fundamental SOP, minterms, POS and maxterms

topics.title: Minimisation and Standard Combinational Circuits
topics.summary: Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps and the Quine-McCluskey method reduce a switching function to fewer gates. Standard combinational circuits include half and full adders, ripple carry adders, multiplexers, demultiplexers, encoders and decoders.
subtopics: Karnaugh maps and grouping adjacent cells
Half adder, full adder and ripple carry adder

topics.title: Sequential Circuits, Counters, Codes and Error Detection
topics.summary: Sequential circuits have memory: their outputs depend on present and past inputs. Flip-flops form registers and counters; computer codes such as BCD, Excess-3 and Gray represent data, and parity and Hamming codes detect and correct transmission errors.
subtopics: Shift registers: SISO, SIPO, PISO and PIPO
Weighted and non-weighted codes: BCD, Excess-3 and Gray
